### [Previewing the Model Hardware Standard](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-hardware-standard-research-preview)

**Anthropic** · 2026-08-28

Anthropic released a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard, a model-agnostic specification that lets AI agents safely interface with physical laboratory and manufacturing equipment.

- Reduces physical hardware integration times from weeks to hours or minutes using a standardized driver layer.
- Uses simple read and write primitives to operate devices like microscopes, liquid handlers, and robotic arms via programmable interfaces.
- Integrates with standard protocols like the Model Context Protocol to make hardware discoverable across networks to any agent harness.
- Embeds natural language tags and safety limits directly into automatically generated reference files to inform agents of physical constraints.

**Why it matters:** It establishes an open framework for AI agents to autonomously orchestrate, monitor, and recover multi-device physical workflows without requiring custom integration code for every tool.

### [Expanding our support for scientists](https://www.anthropic.com/news/expanding-support-for-scientists)

**Anthropic** · 2026-08-28

Anthropic is expanding its scientific support by providing 10,000 discounted or free Claude Team Plan seats and extending its AI for Science grant program to non-biological research fields.

- The new Claude team plan for scientists offers 10,000 seats featuring free standard tiers and $15/month premium tiers with 5x usage limits for verified academic or non-profit principal investigators.
- The AI for Science program provides up to $50,000 in credits per project for compute-heavy research, expanding beyond biology into fields like chemistry and mathematics.
- Biology and chemistry researchers remain restricted to Opus-class models, as Claude Fable models block professional biology and drug development queries due to dual-use risks.
- Anthropic is partnering with the US government to establish a controlled access program allowing life sciences professionals to use Mythos-class models.

**Why it matters:** The expanded plan lowers barriers to advanced compute and LLM integration for academic researchers while maintaining explicit safety restrictions on dual-use biological queries.

### [Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/27/breaking-claude-code-opus-5-auto-mode/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-27

Security researcher Johann Rehberger bypassed Claude Code Opus 5's default auto mode with an 80% success rate using a prompt injection technique that trickles in local file execution via a extracted zip archive.

- The attack tricks Claude Code into downloading and uncompressing a zip file, then executing code that imports base64, which inadvertently triggers a local struct.py file extracted from the archive.
- Auto mode's classifier allowed the creation of the malware process but subsequently blocked Claude's own attempt to execute a cleanup command after detecting the compromise.
- The security vulnerability demonstrates that auto mode classifiers can act as a failure mode by preventing automated agent cleanup actions.

**Why it matters:** Relying on auto mode classifiers for prompt injection defense is insufficient, necessitating strict containerization, VM sandboxing, egress restrictions, and credential isolation for unattended agents.

`prompt-injection` `security` `claude-code` `sandboxing` `ai-safety`
